<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.

<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

<n>2</n> Et edúxit illum a delícto suo, et dedit illi virtútem continéndi ómnia.
<n>3</n> Ab hac ut recéssit iniústus in ira sua, per iram homicídii fratérni depériit.

b.c4aff407d0:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uartodécimo Kaléndas Septémbris Luna décima séptima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>C</h>adómi, in Gállia, sancti Ioánnis Eudes Confessóris, Missionárii Apostólici, Fundatóris Congregatiónis Presbyterórum Iesu et Maríæ necnon Ordinis Moniálium Dóminæ Nostræ a Caritáte, et promotóris litúrgici cultus erga Sacratíssima Christi eiúsque Genitrícis Corda; quem Pius Papa Undécimus fastis Sanctórum adscrípsit.
<h>R</h>omæ Sancti Iúlii, Senatóris et Mártyris; qui, Vitéllio Iúdici tráditus et ab eo in cárcerem trusus, támdiu, iubénte Cómmodo Imperatóre, fústibus cæsus est, donec emítteret spíritum. Ipsíus autem corpus in cœmetério Calepódii via Aurélia, sepúltum fuit.
<h>A</h>nágniæ sancti Magni Epíscopi et Mártyris, qui in persecutióne Décii necátus est.
<h>I</h>n Cilícia natális sancti Andréæ Tribúni et Sociórum mílitum; qui, victória de Persis divínitus adépta, ad fidem Christi convérsi, et hoc nómine accusáti, sub Maximiáno Imperatóre in angústiis Tauri montis ab exércitu Seléuci Prǽsidis trucidáti sunt.
<h>I</h>n Palæstína sancti Timóthei Mártyris, qui in persecutióne Diocletiáni sub Urbáno Prǽside, post multa superáta supplícia, lento igne combústus est. Passi sunt étiam ibídem Thecla et Agápius: illa feris expósita, eárum déntibus laniáta transívit ad Sponsum: Agápius vero, plúrima torménta perpéssus, ad maióra certámina fuit dilátus.
<h>R</h>omæ sancti Xysti Tértii, Papæ et Confessóris.
<h>A</h>pud castrum Bríncolam, in Província, deposítio sancti Ludovíci, ex Ordine Minórum, Epíscopi Tolosáni, vitæ sanctitáte et miráculis clari; cuius corpus, inde Massíliam translátum, in Ecclésia Fratrum Minórum honorífice cónditum fuit, ac póstea Valéntiam, in Hispánia, devéctum est, atque in cathedráli Ecclésia collocátum.
<h>I</h>n pago Sigistérico, in Gállia, beáti Donáti, Presbýteri et Confessóris; qui, ab ipsis usque infántiæ rudiméntis mira Dei grátia prǽditus, anachoréticam vitam multis annis exégit, et miraculórum glória clarus migrávit ad Christum.
<h>I</h>n território Bituricénsi sancti Mariáni Confessóris, cuius virtútes et mirácula beátus Gregórius, Turonénsis Epíscopus, magnis láudibus celebravit.
<h>M</h>ántuæ sancti Rufíni Confessóris.
<h>N</h>orimbérgæ sancti Sebáldi Eremítæ, virtútibus et miráculis præclári, qui Sanctórum catálogo a Martíno Papa Quinto adiéctus est.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.ffec08ed8d:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>A</c>ugust 19th 2027, the 17th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, [in the year 192,] the holy martyr Julius. He was a Senator who was denounced to the judge Vitellius and by him committed to prison, thereafter by command of the Emperor Cornmodus he was beaten with cudgels until he gave up the ghost. His body was buried in the cemetery of Calipodius, upon the Aurelian Way.
<h>A</h>t Anagni, [about the year 250,] the holy martyr Magnus, Bishop [of that see,] who was slain in the persecution under Decius.
<h>I</h>n Cilicia, [about the year 300,] the holy soldiers Andrew the Tribune, and his companions. After obtaining a victory over the Persians by God's help, they were turned to the faith of Christ, and being accused therefore, they were massacred by the army of the President Seleucus in the straits of the Taurus mountain, under the Emperor Maximian.
<h>I</h>n Palestine, the holy martyr Timothy, who after overcoming many torments was burnt at a slow fire, under Urban the President, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian. There suffered there at the same place Thecla and Agapius.
<h>T</h>hecla was thrown to wild beasts, and being rent by them passed away to her Divine Bridegroom. Agapius suffered many tortures, but was kept for greater contendings still.
<h>A</h>t Rome, [in the year 440,] the holy Confessor Pope Sixtus III.
<h>A</h>t the Brignoles, in Provence, [in the year 1297,] holy Louis, of the Order of Friars Minors, Bishop of Toulouse, famous for the holiness of his life and his miracles. His body was carried thence to Marseilles, and is honourably buried there in the church of the Friars Minors.
<h>A</h>t Sisteron, in Gaul, [in the year 535,] the blessed Confessor Donatus, a Priest, who had been from his very infancy marvellously gifted with the grace of God. He lived as a hermit for many years, and passed away to be with Christ, famous for miracles.
<h>I</h>n Berry, [in the sixth century,] the holy Confessor Marian.
<h>A</h>t Mantua, the holy Confessor Rufinus.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Luc. 1:46-55</r>
§00.a228cea5a8
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

b.c83f337eb3:
<h>Canticle: Magnificat</h>

<r>Luke 1:46-55</r>
§00.83742356bc
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

b.6d0ed44df7:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>O</c>mnípotens sempitérne Deus, da nobis fídei, spei et caritátis augméntum: et, ut mereámur ássequi quod promíttis, fac nos amáre quod prǽcipis.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.6044cb3990:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>A</c>lmighty and everlasting God, give unto us the increase of faith, hope, and charity, and that we may worthily obtain that which Thou dost promise, make us to love that which Thou dost command.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Ant.</r> Qui vult veníre post me, ábneget semetípsum, et tollat crucem suam, et sequátur me.
